newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Howard says CPI could have rate implications.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Howard says CPI could have rate implications.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard said on Wednesday that September quarter data was expected to confirm low underlying inflation and that could have an implication for interest rates.

"I don't know what the figure is that's coming out this morning but if the predictions are right, that pattern will continue -- that we have a very low underlying rate of inflation," he told a retirement investment conference.

"Now in the long term, although that might have a short-term implication for interest rates which you may not find as accommodating as people who are borrowing money and paying off something, in the long term if we can lock in very low inflation we will create a more stable environment ...," Howard said.
September quarter consumer price index (CPI) and underlying inflation data are due out at 11.30 a.m. (0130 GMT) today.
Forecasts centre on a quarterly headline CPI rise of just 0.3 percent, bringing the year-on-year rate of 2.5 percent, according to a Reuters survey of economists.
The policy-sensitive underlying inflation rate is forecast at 0.6 percent up on the quarter for an annual rate of 2.5 percent and back within the RBA's two to three percent target.
Both annual rates were at 3.1 percent in the June quarter.
